cited_works.citation: *Products.* \(\gamma_{d+e}\) is the product of \(\gamma_d\) and \(\gamma_e\) (Fubini's theorem, [Fremlin, *Measure Theory*, Volume 2, Theorem 252B](https://www1.essex.ac.uk/maths/people/fremlin/cont25.htm)). For \(A\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) the set \(A\times\mathbb R^e\) has measure \(\gamma_d(A)\) and moment \((z(A),0)\), because \(\int_{\mathbb R^e}y\,d\gamma_e(y)=0\).

*Rotations.* An orthogonal map \(T\) of \(\mathbb R^n\) preserves Lebesgue measure ([Fremlin, *Measure Theory*, Volume 2, Theorem 263A](https://www1.essex.ac.uk/maths/people/fremlin/cont26.htm), with \(|\det T|=1\)) and the Gaussian density, which depends only on \(|x|\). Hence \(\gamma_n(T[A])=\gamma_n(A)\) and \(z(T[A])=Tz(A)\).
